host: madmax Intel Linux, accessed as bullwinkle, nested VMX/KVM
source_provenance: The archive retains the exact candidate patch, including the profile-controlled QEMU egress fix. Target runtime code matches the integrated scheduling change; later desktop-only harness changes are outside this test.
command: make gate-x86_64-smp GUEST_OS=none X86_ROOT_DISK=<isolated seeded full Debian disk> X86_SSH_KEY=<generated identity> X86_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS=<previously console-pinned host key> X86_SSH_PORT=12227 QEMU_TEST_TIMEOUT=3600
proofs: Both managed generations passed pinned Ed25519 public-key SSH, interactive terminal, identity, file/process, network/DNS and package install/execute/remove checks
Both generations exposed CPUs 0 and 1 and passed CPU-affined overlapping x87/SSE workers
Oversized 2052 MiB admission was rejected before both generations without inventory changes
Binary CC creation, console input echo, destruction, fresh-handle recreation, second boot and stale-handle rejection passed
archive_contents: Source patch, artifact hashes, full Make output, console and packet logs, SSH/SMP results, functional-session transcripts and the public host-key provenance. Private SSH identity and disk are excluded.
setup_corrections: An initial extracted-root-only fixture failed its EFI fstab mount; the passing run used the original full partition layout through make seed-guest-root
The native launcher previously restricted outbound traffic, causing the DNS assertion to fail; the passing run used explicit profile-controlled egress
The reused disk required the previously verified host key because cloud-init prints it only on first boot
limits: This is a Debian two-vCPU managed-guest regression on a shared Intel KVM host. It is not a throughput/fairness benchmark, simultaneous multi-guest qualification, or evidence of completed Arch installation or desktop acceptance. VMM, CC and serial scheduling periods remain unchanged.
